chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn Ahmad from Muhammad ibn Isa from Yasin al-Darir from Hariz from Zurarah

That a man from the people of Khurasan came as a pilgrim and he was bald (shaved his head) and did not know how to say the Talbiyah, so Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked about him. He ordered that the Talbiyah be said on his behalf and that a comb be passed over his head, for that suffices for him. And whoever shaves his head, then everything that was prohibited for him becomes permissible, except for women and perfume, unless he performs the Ziyarah. So when he performs Ziyarah and Sa'i, everything becomes permissible for him except women, until he performs the Tawaf al-Nisa'. So when he performs the Tawaf al-Nisa', he has made permissible from everything that was prohibited for him. What indicates that is what he narrated:

key_terms.أَقْرَعَ: Bald or having shaved the head
key_terms.طَوَافَ اَلنِّسَاءِ: Tawaf al-Nisa' (the final circumambulation of the Kaaba)
key_terms.يُلَبِّيَ: To recite the Talbiyah (the specific invocation during Hajj)
key_terms.يُمِرَّ اَلْمُوسَى: To pass a comb over (the head)

ai.seo_question: What are the rulings for a pilgrim who is bald or shaved his head during Hajj?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* via the chain of Zurarah, this hadith clarifies the fiqh of *Hudum* (baldness) and the procedural lifting of *Ihram* restrictions. It establishes that combing the head (*Tamarrud*) suffices for those unable to shave, while detailing the graduated解禁 of prohibitions—permitting food and clothing after head shaving, and all restrictions after *Tawaf al-Nisa’*—reflecting the juristic principle that *Ihram* obligations are tied to specific ritual milestones rather than a single act.
